title: File system
subtitle: How Linux and Windows organize storage — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: How the OS organizes, names, and stores data on disk
cards.example: ext4 on Linux; NTFS on Windows
cards.notes: Unix/Linux and Windows do this in very different ways.

cards.meaning: ext2, ext3, ext4, ReiserFS, XFS, Btrfs, and others
cards.notes: Linux supports many file system types.

cards.meaning: One tree starting at / — every file lives somewhere under it
cards.notes: Even files on a second disk appear under the same root; there is no drive letter.

cards.meaning: Extra disks or partitions attach onto a directory in the single tree
cards.notes: You do not get a new drive letter — e.g. /mnt/data or /home.

cards.meaning: Not required — the kernel does not decide file type from the name
cards.notes: run.sh is a script only if it has execute permission and a shebang (or you pass it to a shell).

cards.front: What makes a file executable on Linux
cards.meaning: The execute bit (chmod +x) and, for scripts, the interpreter in the shebang
cards.notes: Extensions like .conf, .service, .log are for humans and tools; the OS does not require them.
Modern Windows also has ReFS; this course sticks to the classic three.

cards.meaning: Storage shown as A: through Z: — each disk/partition can be a new root
cards.notes: A second disk is often a new letter (D:), not a mount under one tree.

cards.meaning: System behavior depends on the extension
cards.notes: Contrast with Linux: content + permissions, not the name.

cards.front: How storage is shown: Linux vs Windows
cards.meaning: Linux: one tree at /. Windows: drive letters A:–Z:
cards.notes: Interview-ready comparison for mounting Windows shares too.

cards.meaning: Turn on the execute bit — Linux does not care about .sh
cards.notes: Extension alone does not make a file runnable.

cards.meaning: Attach a disk/partition onto a directory in the single tree
cards.notes: Second disk becomes a directory under /, not a new letter.

cards.meaning: Show block devices and their mount points
cards.notes: Quick view of disks, partitions, and where they are mounted.
